lm_output: "But one thing the facts cry out, and it can be clear, as they say, even to a blind man, that often through the translator's clumsiness or inattention the Greek has been wrongly rendered; often the original meaning of the sentence has been lost; often it has been necessary to choose among several possible meanings, and then only one has been translated, the wrong one; often whole thoughts have been dropped, because the translator did not understand them, or because he understood them too well and was afraid of them, and sometimes because they were superfluous for the reader of the translation, though they were of the greatest importance for the reader of the original; often translations contain interpolations, that have been inserted by the translator, in order to make the translation clearer, or in order to make it possible for the reader to understand it at all, or simply because the translator did not realize that he was making an interpolation; often words and sentences are transposed, so that a thought which in the original follows later will precede, and vice versa; often the style of the translation is different from that of the original, because the translator wants to show his own beautiful style, and often because he does not know how to do it any other way; often the translator invents something himself, and then it is no longer a translation, just as a house which a builder builds differently from what the client ordered is no longer the house which the client ordered. And all these things, and many others, are committed by the translator, not because he wants to sin, God forbid, but because he is a human being, and therefore imperfect, and because he does not always understand the original, and because he cannot always express in one language what he understands in another, and because he is often in a hurry, and because he is often tired, and because he is often bored, and because he often wants to finish the translation quickly in order to start a new one, and because he often wants to go to sleep, and because he often wants to eat, and because he often has other things to do.
